review_type: Author mathematical, numerical and instructional review; no independent academic certification

reviewed.reasoning: Checked finite convex-combination induction, intersection/affine/epigraph rules, relative-domain interpretation, nearest-point separation with explicit closedness/compactness, weak duality signs and concavity, finite gaps versus distance, Slater sufficiency/domain/value/attainment distinctions, convex KKT and saddle certificates, nonattained dual example, perturbation bounds, epsilon-based value convexity, kink subgradients, implicit quantity responses and global payoff monotonicity. General Slater proof is explicitly distinguished from its geometric explanation. Discrete nonconvex-domain example explicitly exhibits an attained positive duality gap and its convex-hull relaxation.
reviewed.arithmetic: Independent exact fraction reconstruction of completing-square identities, primal/dual values and residuals across regimes, target and equality exercises, disk separation, kink multipliers, failed-qualification sequence, payoff/capacity responses and distance bound; finite difference equality sensitivity cross-check.
reviewed.solutions: All eight prompts solved with proof or calculation and relevant assumptions. Global examples cross-checked in original objectives rather than merely in stationarity equations.
reviewed.instruction: Separates infimum from attainment, domain restrictions from relaxed constraints, shadow values from quantity responses, ordinary from one-sided derivatives, and mathematical model response from empirical causality. Uses prior calculus, geometry and KKT tools; compactness proof remains explicitly a Chapter 10 prerequisite followup.
reviewed.sources: Official Stanford lecture index and linked author slides retrieved; convex epigraph material and duality relative-domain/perturbation sections inspected. References are method and further-study routes, not manuscript certification. Problems and examples are original.
reviewed.structure: Two worked examples, eight exercises with full solutions, teach-back and delayed check, stated scope and method-specific references.

limitations: Slater is stated with a geometric explanation; a general separation-based theorem proof belongs to the later graduate convex-analysis treatment.
